verdict.rationale: Clerk acts as an OAuth provider with scoped access for third-party apps (clerk-docs-10/44), and a changelog entry on custom OAuth scopes explicitly targets MCP clients (clerk-docs-55). The eve guide adds gating of tool calls against the caller's permissions and scopes (clerk-docs-16), and Clerk ships a standards-based device grant flow (clerk-docs-52). However, no evidence shows a documented guide for protecting your own MCP server or for MCP-spec compliance, and the MCP-scopes evidence is only a truncated changelog line. Missing for 10: an explicit guide to putting a Clerk OAuth flow in front of a user's MCP server, evidence of MCP-spec elements (protected-resource metadata, dynamic client registration), documented verification of OAuth access tokens on the resource server, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
